finding2_rewrite.what_changed: rev2 finding 2 asserted as a CROSS-ASSET generalisation that the SE understatement comes mainly from the 1/(2 sqrt m) asymptotic formula. With arm C making the mean-estimation factor visible, that holds for only 2 of 5 assets (VIX, SPY); QQQ and N225 are mean_estimation-dominant and TW0050 is break_location-dominant. README 6.4 finding 2 is rewritten as a downgrade, not an extension.
finding2_rewrite.what_survives: All three sd factors exceed 1.0 for every asset, so the conclusion that the published SE IS understated (1.21-1.33x) is unchanged. Only the ATTRIBUTION was downgraded.

dominant_factor_robustness.method: Gaussian approximation 1/sqrt(2(n-1)); the artifact stores only per-arm mean/sd (no per-replication draws), so no bootstrap was possible. This is an order-of-magnitude sanity check, NOT a formal test.
dominant_factor_robustness.caveat: SPY's top-two gap is 0.31%, roughly an order of magnitude BELOW the ~3.2% crude MC SE, so its 'asymptotic_formula' label is effectively a coin flip. Strictly only VIX has a robustly dominant asymptotic-formula factor. This makes the downgrade stronger, not weaker, and is recorded in README 6.4 finding 2 and scope limit 5.
